page.layout: One page of text, one column. At the top, a woodcut ornamental strip (not text). Below it, the centred title in capitals and roman, two lines. Then the body paragraph with a woodcut initial H. Margin notes in the right margin. A signature mark "A" centred at the foot.

main_text.head: IOHANNES RAINOLDVS ALVMNIS Anglicorum seminariorum Romae & rhemis.
main_text.p: Hasce iam alteras vobis literas scribo, dilecti, quibus mentem vestram per commonefactionem excito. Sinceram quidem mentem ait S.{a}a 2.Pet.3.18[?] Petrus; laudans pietatem eorum, quos secunda epistola sua excitat: quippe sanctis scribit,{b}b 1.Pet.1.1. sorti-tis[?] aquè pretiosam fidem cum Apostolis per iustitiam Dei nostri & Servatoris Iesu Christi. Atque utinam mihi perinde licuisset ab integra illius sententia secundam hanc ad vos ordiri, ac priorem licuit ab integra S. {c}c Rom.10.18[?] Pauli: Fratres, propensa quidem voluntas cordis mei & deprecatio ad Deum super Israel est ad salutem; testor enim de ipsis, eos zelum Dei habere, sed non ex notitia. Verùm hic defectus notitiae scientiaeque, ut a Paulo in {d}d Rom.9.4[?] fratribus cognatis suis secundum carnem, sic a me in vobis merito notatus, impedit ne illius sinceritatis laude, quae fidelibus Dei servis tributa est, vos adhuc afficiam. Etenim {e}e 1.Cor.5.8. sinceritas cum veritate copulatur, & permistioni fermenti opponitur, non in moribus solùm, sed etiam in {f}f Matt.16. ver.6.&12. doctrina unde Philippesibus optatū {g}g Phil.1.9. redundare in cognitione & omni sensu, dignoscere quae discrepant, ut sint sinceri. Quanquam, si {h}h Aphthon progymnas[?]mata in χρείας Diogenes, quum puerum indecorè se gerentem conspiceret, paedagogum eius percussit haud iniuria, dicens, Cur sic instituis? cor-

page.notes: Uncertain readings: the first word of the second-paragraph line "sorti-tis" (the printed first letter could be f or s; the Vulgate of 2 Pet. 1:1 suggests "sortitis"); "Rom.10.18" and the letter after "S." before "Pauli" are hard to read, and the margin letter may be c or e; the reference "Rom.9.4" is partly illegible; the Greek word after "in" in note h is faint; "progymnasmata" in note h is partly illegible. The marginal note "a 2.Pet.3.18" is uncertain. Show-through marks in the right margin and the ornament strip above the title are not transcribed. The paragraph continues on the next page after "cor-".
